key_insight: The study proposes an ontology-integrated NLP system to automatically identify and stage heart failure and COPD symptom severity from clinical notes using NYHA and GOLD classifications.
clinical_relevance: If successful, it could help surface severity information hidden in unstructured EHR text for better decision support, surveillance, and retrospective analysis.
method: Hybrid NLP pipeline combining rule-based extraction and Bi-LSTM-CRF sequence labeling
SNOMED-CT ontology mapping for semantic normalization and explainable staging
Text preprocessing includes tokenization, lemmatization, dependency parsing, abbreviation expansion, and negation detection
evidence_signal: The protocol plans to test the framework on about 1,000 de-identified notes from public datasets and evaluate it with precision, recall, F1-score, Cohen’s kappa, sensitivity, and specificity.
watch_item: Because this is a study protocol using heterogeneous public datasets, real-world performance and portability may be limited without local validation and robust annotation quality.
paper_title: NLP Framework for Automated Symptom Severity Staging in Heart Failure and COPD Clinical Notes Using Ontology Integration: A Study Protocol
